item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Portrait Photo Into Story Frame

turns.text: Can you make this fit a 9:16 Instagram story? Keep all my hair and shoulders—use a blurred copy of the photo behind it if needed. No text.

item.tests: Tests creating a vertical story from a square portrait without clipping the person or distorting the photo.

answer_sheet.Framing: Keep all the hair and shoulders visible in the original photo.
answer_sheet.Filling extra space: A blurred copy of the same photo behind the intact portrait is fine.
answer_sheet.Text and retouching: No text or retouching; preserve my appearance.

must_haves: The delivered image has a 9:16 vertical frame.
The sharp foreground portrait shows the same woman, curly hair and sweater as the attachment.
No hair or shoulder area visible in the source is lost.
The portrait is not stretched or squeezed.
Any added background space uses a blurred version of the source photo, with no text.

turns.text: Can you help me make this pic fit properly without cutting off parts of me? I always get a little nervous about how a portrait will look once it’s been resized. What I need is a 9:16 Instagram story, with all my hair and shoulders kept in the frame. If you need to fill the extra space, you can use a blurred copy of the same photo behind it. I’m probably overthinking it because I’ve had awkward crops before. Please don’t add any text.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make your story image. Your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits for an image edit. I tried twice, the second time with the cheapest free-plan model (about 5 credits), and the account turned down both requests. Nothing was made and no credits were spent.

**What you need:** your photo is square, so for a 9:16 story it should be shown at full width, uncropped, with a blurred copy of the same photo filling the space above and below. That way none of your hair or shoulders gets cut off.

**To get it done:**
- **With Magic Hour:** once you've topped up your credits or your free credits renew, tell me and I'll run it again with the same settings: 9:16, the whole photo unchanged in the center, a blurred background and no text.
- **Do it yourself now:** in Canva or CapCut, start a 1080×1920 canvas. Add your photo twice. Stretch the first copy to fill the whole canvas and set its blur to high. Put the second copy on top at full width (1080×1080), centered, and don't crop it. Export without adding any text.
- **Instagram on its own:** if you post the square photo straight to a story without zooming in, Instagram shows the whole thing and fills the gaps with a colour gradient instead of a blur. Pinching to zoom is usually what causes the awkward crops, so leave it at its normal size.

You're not overthinking it. Avoiding crops is exactly why the full-width layout is the right choice for this photo.

Fill the empty space above and below with a heavily blurred, enlarged copy of the same photo (soft-focus green park background) as a backdrop. Do not change her face, hair, expression or clothing. No text, no captions, no logos, no borders.
